loci.name: ffews-last-mile-atlas-role
loci.one_line: Given riverine forecasting gains but documented last-mile failures (2024 floods, 2026 Bhotekoshi), what can a static public site realistically add to warning dissemination versus risk misleading users or duplicating BIPAD?
loci.rationale: Reducing-flood-casualties note and Ncell SMS note report deaths falling 166 to 27 and 4.4M alerts; Sixteen-minutes and Missing-on-early-warning notes show accurate alerts still yielding ~250 deaths, Nepali-only generic SMS and 5h-late posts. Corpus does not say where a read-only atlas fits (lead time, scenario vs live, disclaimers, Nepali-first alerts).

opposing_positions.position: Forecasting/SMS system has succeeded; fatalities fell
Dissemination still fails for flash floods, GLOFs and transboundary events

suggested_searches: Nepal early warning last mile evaluation 2024 floods
community-based early warning Nepal evaluation digital tools
transboundary flood alert Nepal China India data sharing

loci.name: cap-feed-interoperability-roadmap
loci.one_line: Should the Atlas ingest/emit CAP (and align with BIPAD/WMO SWIC) and what feeds and formats are actually available and stable for the scraper?
loci.rationale: CAP spec, SWIC 3.0 and WMO Nepal notes show CAP implementation agreed Apr 2025, cell broadcast costed but unprocured; the BIPAD impact-based module note hints at APIs but corpus does not establish which DHM/BIPAD/NEMRC endpoints are machine-readable, licensed, or stable for a daily scraper.
suggested_searches: Nepal Common Alerting Protocol implementation plan 2025

loci.name: reach-offline-lowbandwidth-bilingual
loci.one_line: Who can actually use the Atlas: how do conflicting connectivity estimates, language/literacy and accessibility evidence change priorities (offline PWA, PMTiles, SMS/print, voice, Nepali-first, a11y)?
loci.rationale: Batch9 gives MICS 82% household internet vs ITU 48.4% individual use; Karnali 68.5%. Offline PMTiles and accessibility checklist notes hint at solutions but not Nepal-specific evidence of which delivery mode wins for at-risk, low-literacy groups.

opposing_positions.position: Connectivity is high (82% households), web-first is fine
Individual use ~48-56%; large offline/low-bandwidth minority, so web-only misses at-risk users

suggested_searches: Nepal digital literacy disaster information rural Karnali
PWA offline disaster map low bandwidth evaluation

loci.name: risk-map-uncertainty-communication
loci.one_line: How should scenario maps and printable reports show uncertainty without crisp safe/unsafe lines or false reassurance?
loci.rationale: Natural-frequency and isarithmic formats improve comprehension (frontiers note, public-understanding note) but benefit fades for rare high-consequence events and hard boundaries carry legal weight; L'Aquila (r-e-g-u-l-a-r-p-a-p-e-r). Directly bears on the Atlas scenario models and print reports.

opposing_positions.position: Frequency formats and gradient maps improve comprehension
Benefit fades for rare events; hard boundaries and reassurance risk harm

suggested_searches: hypothetical scenario map public misinterpretation as forecast

loci.name: sustainability-maintenance-model
loci.one_line: What governance, funding and maintenance model keeps a volunteer static atlas and its daily scraper alive and current?
loci.rationale: GeoNode sustained via community (open-data-for-resilience-initiative) versus OpenDRI finding no project self-sustaining and data going stale (opendri-7-sustaining); crowd mapping note and OSM Nepal notes suggest community routes. Scraper fragility against government site changes is a practical risk.

opposing_positions.position: No project self-sustaining; data goes stale

suggested_searches: government data scraper breakage staleness indicator open data portals

skip_loci.reason: Hazard science, left to analyst a.
